audience: OLEANDER design review / portfolio integration teams
question: How can a relational route network communicate route/service/return authority before optional reading content without pretending to be a surveyed map?
primary_claim: Route / Service / Return remain structurally legible while optional reading stays subordinate and skippable.
source_authority: C04 C22 relational drawing/data package v3.0
truth_boundary: RELATIONAL / NTS / NOT GEOREFERENCED / FIELD OBSERVED=0 / FIELD MEASURED=0 / G1F HOLD / NO_PROMOTION
visual_form: asymmetric analytical poster + relational node-edge field + evidence strip
data_transform: role-priority remapping only; no new factual topology claim

encoding_channels.stroke_color: route vs conditional vs return semantic role; not evidence by color alone

scale_rule: NTS; no metric axis; no geographic scale
secondary_context: optional reading branches and companion nodes
grid_alignment_rule: single 1920x1080 surface; asymmetric narrative field + dominant analytical field + full-width evidence strip
annotation_budget: only claim, role, boundary, key node labels, evidence-finding-consequence; no full node exposition
mid_read: service anchors, optional branches, return spine and closure
near_read: source-traced vs diagrammatic vs field-open tags and evidence strip
signature: return spine is a distinct, continuously readable relational layer without becoming a fake single itinerary
accessibility_equivalent: NETWORK_DATA_v0.1.json + explicit labels; semantics are not color-only
